messages:
maria: bringing up heron-3b-q4 on dedicated for long-context tests. seeing reproducible KV cache misalignment after prefill + resume on sequences > 32k tokens. filing here before I start a bisect.

aj: can you paste the minimal repro? curious whether it's rope scaling or an index overflow.

maria: repro below (super small). run with our local serve binary (latest main) + int4 checkpoint. noticed output tokens start repeating ~28000 tokens in.

```bash
# load model, prefill a long system prompt then resume generation
python serve_repro.py --model heron-3b-q4 --prefill-file long_prompt.txt --resume-steps 1024 --max-tokens 32768
```

and a snippet from the decode log: (we dump kv indices)

```
[2026-03-19 14:02:10] prefill: kv_write start idx_range=[0, 16384)
[2026-03-19 14:02:13] resume: kv_read start idx=16384 expected_next=16384
[2026-03-19 14:12:05] decode: kv_read start idx=32768 expected_next=32768
[2026-03-19 14:12:20] WARNING: kv_index_wrapping: observed idx 64 while expected 32768
[2026-03-19 14:12:20] generation: repeated token beam[0]=\"the\" x12
```

maria: suspect either (A) RoPE phase scaling mismatch between prefill and resume kernels or (B) truncation/tiling logic in the KV ring buffer incorrectly wrapping an absolute index into a small window.

aj: first thought: do we apply the same rotary scaling factor when we quantize weights? sometimes quantization packs change scale inference path. check kernel flags: USE_ROTARY_PHASE_RESCALE in runtime config.

devin: is this only on q4 ints? can you repro on fp16 to rule out quantization-specific mempack corruption?

maria: good call — fp16 run attached was clean on same binary. quant4 shows the misalignment. so leaning quant path regression.

bench-bot: run_id=3032109876-1 | model=heron-3b-q4 | fp16_baseline=PASS | q4_misalign=FAIL | p50_latency_ms=48 | notes=repeat_after_28000_tokens

natalie: if fp16 is clean, maybe the int4 kernel's memcpy/copy stride when stitching shards truncates the 32-bit index to 16-bit somewhere. can you dump the raw kv_index values right before the memcpy?

maria: done. attaching a short dump excerpt below (index, low16, high16):

```
kv_idx_dump[0:8]:
  32760 -> low16=32760 high16=0
  32761 -> low16=32761 high16=0
  32762 -> low16=32762 high16=0
  64    -> low16=64    high16=0  # <-- corrupted here in q4 run
```

maria: note: high16 still zero which suggests truncation rather than overflow.

aj: hmm that points at a cast to uint16_t in the quant path. search for any index_t -> uint16 conversions in int4 memcpy/pack. I'll grep.

devin: also check RoPE application codepaths: we have an alternate fast-path for quantized KV that uses fused-rope kernel. if that assumes contiguous absolute indices < WINDOW_SIZE it might rewrite indices to remapped positions.

maria: quick workaround found: disable the fused memcpy (RUNTIME_FLAG_DISABLE_FUSED_COPY=1) and the q4 run now resumes correctly (no index truncation). so definitely in the fused quant path.

ci-bot: opened issue #8342: "heron-3b-q4 fused-copy kv-index truncation" assigned to @aj, priority=P0. logs attached.

aj: I'll take the issue. initial plan: add index-type audit in fused_copy, add asserts to catch >16-bit index, and run the int4 unit tests with longprefill.

natalie: also recommend an eval harness change: add a long-context q4 smoke to the onboarding checklist. current onboarding only runs up to 16k tokens, bump to 48k for quantized variants.

maria: agreed — I'll open a PR to expand model-onboard.yml and add a long-context q4 job to the nightly matrix (heron-3b-q4-longctx-smoke). also adding a quick debugger script that toggles the fused copy flag and dumps raw kv indices.

aj: for the code fix: minimal change is to force index to 32-bit in fused_copy and remove implicit casts. but we should also add CI coverage: small integration that writes >32k indices into the KV ring buffer and verifies readback identity across quant/unquant paths.

devin: sounds good. if the fused kernel relied on 16-bit indices for on-GPU packing efficiency we should measure perf impact when switching to 32-bit indices. maybe use a tiled 32-bit packing instead of naive 16-bit truncation.

maria: perf tradeoff note: disabling fused copy increased p50 by ~6ms in bench run, acceptable as a short-term fallback. long-term we want correctness + vectorized 32-bit copy.

natalie: I can follow up on the onboarding docs and runbook. we should document the binary flag, repro steps, and the detection heuristic (repeated token bursts after ~28k).

maria: created branch: fix/fused-copy-index-audit, pushing logs and a unit-test harness. will ping when PR is up.

aj: thanks — prioritizing the patch. once merged, run the expanded onboarding matrix and mark the model as verified for dedicated long-context.

maria: thanks all. leaving the thread open for CI results.
